## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The sutta sets out the theme of practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammapaṭipanna*).

 Within the Pali Canon, verse parallels are found in the Dhammapada (Dhp 364) and the Theragāthā (Thag 17.3, the *Ānandattheragāthā*). In non-Pali corpora, parallels occur widely in the Dharmapada and Udānavarga traditions: the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 51–90, *Bhikhuvagga*), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 216–238, *Śaraṇavagga*), Sanskrit recensions of the Udānavarga (UV 32 and UVS 32, *Bhikṣuvarga*), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 32), and three Chinese Dharmapada/Udānavarga translations (T 210.34, T 212.33, and T 213.32). Another narrative parallel is attested in the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu* (San Lo Mvu 107, *The Jātaka of Asthisena*).

None of the gathered passages from secondary literature treat Iti 86 directly, instead referencing the PTS page number 86 of the *Itivuttaka* (which belongs to Iti 89) or examining the term *dhammānudhammapaṭipanna* in the context of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya*.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
